text: A system with n n independent components which functions if and only if at least k k of the components function is a k k out of n n system Parallel systems are out of n n systems and series systems are n n out of n n systems If p p p n p is the vector of component reliabilities for the n n components then h k p h is the reliability function of the system It is shown that h k p h is Schurconvex in n n n n p This Theorem is compared with a result on Schurconvexity and concavity by Gleser which in turn extends work of Hoeffding

author: Frank Proschan
text: We study the model in which a set of spares is available for redundancy in a coherent system In some circumstances parallel or active redundancy is used to improve the reliability of the system while in others series redundancy is used to improve a different measure of utility Hence we define the two concepts of parallel and series redundancy importance for components in a coherent system relative to an available set of redundant spares These measures of importance are compared with the structural importance and reliability importance of a component due to Birnbaum Various results for the optimal allocation of redundant spares are given with particular reference to k out of n systems and modules of coherent systems

author: Frank Proschan
text: We develop a unified theory for obtaining stochastic rearrangement inequalities and show how this theory may be applied in statistical contexts such as ranking problems hypothesis testing contamination models and optimal assembly of systems

author: Frank Proschan
text: This paper introduces and explores a new class of inequalities termed Stochastic Rearrangement Inequalities which extend traditional rearrangement inequalities by incorporating stochastic processes By analyzing the behavior of random variables subjected to rearrangement operations we establish novel results that characterize the probabilistic orderings of these variables The key contributions include the formulation of stochastic rearrangement inequalities for a variety of classes of random variables including independent and identically distributed iid variables and those with specific dependence structures We employ tools from probability theory and measure theory to derive our results revealing connections to classical inequalities in both deterministic and stochastic contexts Additionally applications of these inequalities in fields such as statistical physics economics and information theory are discussed illustrating their versatility and significance in understanding the behavior of systems under uncertainty The findings not only deepen the theoretical foundations of rearrangement inequalities but also provide practical tools for researchers working with stochastic models

author: Frank Proschan
text: The lOO percentile residual life function at time x is defined to be the lOO percentile of the remaining life given survival up to time x Joe and Proschan b develop tests for testing the alternatives representing decreasing percentile residual life DPRL and the property new better than used with respect to the lOO percentile NBUP In this paper tests are developed for DPRL l and NBUP l alternatives where DPRL l is the class of life distributions which are DPRL distributions for all a if and for all if and NBUP l is similarly defined When the DPRL l class of life distributions corresponds to the increasing failure rate class and the NBUP l class of life distributions corresponds to the new better than used class and the test statistics are respectively asymptotically equivalent to the Hollander and Proschan test statistics for decreasing mean residual life and new better than used in expectation alternatives

author: Frank Proschan
text: SUMMARY In this paper we develop tests for alternatives representing decreasing mean residual life and the property new better than used in expectation The decreasing mean residual life test statistic V is new and critical constants and a largesample approximation are obtained to make the test readily applicable The new better than used in expectation statistic K is shown to be equivalent to the total time on test statistic the latter is ordinarily viewed as a test statistic for alternatives of increasing failure rate Consistency and asymptotic relative efficiency results are obtained for the tests based on V and K These results lead to a reinterpretation of the total time on test statistic as a test statistic for classes of alternatives larger than the increasing failure rate class and including the new better than used in expectation class

author: Frank Proschan
text: In this paper we investigate statistical methods for assessing the mean residual life MRL a vital concept in reliability theory and survival analysis that provides insights into the expected remaining lifespan of an entity given its current age We propose a suite of robust statistical tests designed to evaluate MRL functions across a range of distributions focusing on empirical MRL estimates derived from censored and uncensored data Utilizing both parametric and nonparametric approaches we derive asymptotic distributions for the test statistics and conduct simulations to assess the power and size of our proposed tests under various scenarios including differing sample sizes and censoring mechanisms Our findings reveal that the proposed tests maintain good power characteristics even in the presence of data irregularities We demonstrate practical applications of these tests using realworld datasets providing insights into their applicability in fields such as medicine engineering and economics Overall this work contributes to the existing literature by offering comprehensive methodologies for testing hypotheses related to mean residual life enhancing the toolkit available for practitioners in survival analysis and reliability assessment

author: Frank Proschan
text: In this paper we introduce a novel framework for understanding and quantifying associations among multiple variables through the concept of generalized association While conventional association measures typically address bivariate relationships our approach extends these concepts to encompass multivariate scenarios providing a rigorous statistical foundation for analyzing interactions within highdimensional data We develop a set of generalized association metrics that capture both linear and nonlinear dependencies enabling researchers to uncover complex relationships that traditional methods may overlook Through extensive simulations and realdata applications we demonstrate the utility of our proposed metrics in various contexts such as psychometrics genomics and environmental studies We also present a comprehensive set of tools for visualizing multivariate associations including scatterplot matrices and heatmaps which facilitate the interpretation of intricate relationships among multiple variables Our findings suggest that generalized association metrics significantly enhance the detectability of underlying patterns in multivariate datasets paving the way for more informed decisionmaking in fields reliant on complex data analysis This work lays the groundwork for future research and methodology enhancements in the field of multivariate statistics

author: Frank Proschan
text: The analysis of reliability growth in systems composed of dependent components is critical for accurate predictability of performance and lifespan in engineered systems This paper presents a novel reliability growth model that accounts for dependencies among components aiming to enhance the understanding of how interactions influence failure rates and reliability improvements over time We introduce a new framework that amalgamates traditional reliability growth modeling techniques with advanced statistical methods suitable for dependent variables such as copulas and survival analysis The model is validated using simulation studies and realworld data from complex systems illustrating its applicability in diverse fields such as aerospace automotive and electronics engineering Through sensitivity analyses we assess the impact of component dependence structures on overall system reliability providing insights into optimal testing and maintenance strategies Our findings highlight the importance of considering component dependencies in reliability assessments ultimately contributing to more robust and resilient system designs This work lays the groundwork for future research into more complex reliability scenarios and offers a comprehensive approach for practitioners aiming to enhance system performance

author: Frank Proschan
text: In the realm of engineering reliability the strategic allocation of spare components in coherent systems is imperative for optimizing system performance and minimizing downtime This paper explores the interplay between redundancy the criticality of components and spare allocation through a comprehensive statistical framework We define redundancy importance metrics for coherent systems allowing us to quantify the impact of specific component failures on overall system reliability Utilizing advanced statistical methods including probabilistic modeling and simulation techniques we analyze various spare allocation strategies within a range of coherent architectures Our findings reveal significant insights into how the distribution of spares can be effectively tailored to enhance system resilience Furthermore we present case studies that illustrate the application of our proposed methodologies in realworld scenarios demonstrating how targeted spare allocation can lead to substantial improvements in system availability and lifespan This research not only contributes to the theoretical understanding of redundancy and spare management but also offers practical guidelines for engineers aiming to optimize reliability in complex systems

author: Frank Proschan
text: In the classical theory of competing risks as well as in many reliability models and incomplete data problems it is assumed that A the risks ie the random variables of interest are independent and that A death does not result from simultaneous causes Employing our probabilistic solution to a related problem in probability modelling we obtain strongly consistent estimators for the unobservable marginal distributions of interest These estimators are analogous to those of Kaplan and Meier and are appropriate when the assumptions of independence and no simultaneous causes of death fail to hold We show how our methods can be used to unify and simplify the nonparametric approach toward estimation in the competing risks model As a consequence we obtain an elementary proof of the strong consistency of the KaplanMeier estimator Our results extend and simplify the work of Peterson and Desu and Narula

author: Frank Proschan
text: In reliability engineering KoutofN systems serve as fundamental models for assessing the performance and dependability of complex systems comprised of interconnected components This paper delves into the reliability characteristics of KoutofN systems focusing on both theoretical foundations and practical implications We present a comprehensive analysis of the systems reliability function incorporating various failure distributions and dependencies among components By employing advanced statistical techniques we derive explicit expressions for the reliability and failure probabilities and we explore the impact of component redundancy on overall system performance Furthermore we utilize Monte Carlo simulations to validate our theoretical results and provide insights into the systems behavior under diverse operational conditions Our findings demonstrate that the reliability of KoutofN systems is significantly influenced by the choice of components and their arrangement revealing optimal strategies for design and maintenance This study contributes to a deeper understanding of reliability metrics in engineering and informs decisionmaking processes regarding system design in various applications from telecommunications to aerospace engineering We conclude with implications for future research and potential advancements in reliability assessment methodologies

author: Frank Proschan
text: Earlier papers have shown how to convert competing risk models involving dependent random variables into models involving only independent random variables while simultaneously preserving the distribution of the minimum and the probabilities of the various failure patterns In the present paper we consider a sequence of such conversions occurring at successive points in chronological time in which the independent random variables are becoming stochastically larger We obtain results which essentially demonstrate that the limiting distributions in the sequence of dependent models correctly correspond to the limiting distributions in the sequence of independent models These results have applications in reliability growth models and in biomedical competing risk models in which the competing risks are increasing with age in these models dependency is permitted among the random variables

author: Frank Proschan
text: Association of random variables is generalized by considering increasing functions on certain partially ordered spaces Generalized association enjoys many of the basic properties possessed by association An essential connection links the two notions Generalized association is inherited under certain mixing processes Applications of this result follow for absolute value ordering unimodal ordering and linear ordering of the real numbers

author: Frank Proschan
text: AbstractResidual life an important concept in survival analysis and reliability theory refers to the expected remaining lifetime of an entity conditioned on its survival up to a certain time This paper presents a comprehensive series of statistical tests designed to evaluate key properties of residual life such as monotonicity independence and the existence of memoryless behavior We first establish formal definitions and foundational properties of residual life distributions followed by the introduction of various hypothesis tests tailored to assess these characteristics Utilizing both parametric and nonparametric methodologies we derive test statistics and their corresponding distributions under the null hypotheses We also incorporate simulation studies to evaluate the power and robustness of the proposed tests across different settings and sample sizes The practical applicability of our methods is demonstrated through a series of case studies including reliability data from engineering systems and survival data from health studies Our findings provide valuable insights into the residual life properties offering a statistical framework that can enhance the understanding of timetoevent data in various domains Ultimately this work contributes to improving the assessment of failure risks and lifetimes in critical applications

author: Frank Proschan
text: In the realm of survival analysis accurately estimating dependent life lengths is crucial for understanding the dynamics of competing risks This paper presents a novel statistical framework for estimating life lengths when multiple dependent risks are present extending traditional survival models that often assume independence among competing events We introduce a joint modeling approach that combines elements of copula theory and frailty models enabling us to capture the inherent dependence between competing risks while providing robust estimates of survival probabilities and hazard functions We apply our methodology to realworld datasets from healthcare studies where the risks of different medical conditions interact demonstrating the effectiveness of our approach in revealing nuanced insights into patient outcomes Our findings highlight the importance of accounting for dependency in risk estimation and we discuss implications for both statistical methodology and practical applications in fields such as biostatistics and actuarial science Ultimately this work contributes to a deeper understanding of competing risks and offers enhanced tools for researchers and practitioners aiming to inform decisionmaking in complex risk environments

author: Frank Proschan
text: In this paper we obtain characterizations of large classes of nonparametric life distributions such as the increasing decreasing failure rate increasing decreasing failure rate average new better worse than used etc classes The methods used differ from the usual functional equation methods used for the far more common characterizations of parametric families of life distributions

author: Frank Proschan
text: Uniform stochastic orderings of random variables are expressed as total positivity TP of density survival and distribution functions The orderings are called uniform because each is a stochastic order that persists under conditioning to a family of intervals for example the family consisting of all intervals of the form x This paper is concerned with the preservation of uniform stochastic ordering under convolution mixing and the formation of coherent systems A general TP result involving preservation of total positivity under integration is presented and applied to convolutions and mixtures of distribution and survival functions Log concavity of distribution survival and density functions characterizes distributions that preserve the various orderings under convolution Likewise distributions that preserve orderings under mixing are characterized by TP distribution and survival functions

author: Frank Proschan
text: This paper explores the interplay between moment inequalities and geometric probability within the framework of arrangement increasing functions We begin by defining arrangement increasing functions and their significance in probability theory and moment analysis By leveraging combinatorial techniques and properties of these functions we derive a series of moment inequalities that provide new insights into the behavior and relationships of random variables Furthermore we establish geometric probability inequalities that connect the intrinsic geometric structure of arrangement increasing functions with probabilistic measures Our results bridge the gap between discrete and continuous probability frameworks extending classical inequality results and offering new interpretations in the context of stochastic processes We conclude by discussing potential applications of these inequalities in fields such as statistical inference risk assessment and information theory emphasizing their relevance in the analysis of complex probabilistic models

author: Frank Proschan
text: This is Part I of a twopart paper the purpose of this twopart paper is a to develop new concepts and techniques in the theory of majorization and Schur functions and b to obtain fruitful applications in probability and statistics The main theorem of Part I states that if f x x n f is Schurconcave and if x is totally positive of order and satisfies the semigroup property for y x y xd x where is Lebesgue measure on or counting measure on then h n n i x i f x x n d x d x n h is also Schurconcave This theorem is then applied to obtain renewal theory results moment inequalities and shock model properties

author: Frank Proschan
text: Let T T denote the life length of a series system of n n components having respective life lengths T T n T not necessarily independent We give necessary and sufficient conditions for the existence of a set of independent random variables I This extends the results of Miller while using more elementary methods

author: Frank Proschan
text: In this paper we present conditions on the likelihood function and on the prior distribution which permit us to assess the effect of the sample on the posterior distribution Our work is inspired by Whitt J Amer Statist Assoc and is based on the notions of multivariate totally positive and strongly multivariate reverse rule functions introduced and studied by Karlin and Rinott a b

author: Frank Proschan
text: In this paper we investigate the Decreasing In Transposition Property DITP of overlapping sums within the framework of statistical analysis The DITP refers to the phenomenon where the rearrangement of summands in overlapping sums leads to a reduction in their overall value a property significant in various applications including econometrics risk assessment and resource allocation We provide a comprehensive theoretical framework that explicates the conditions under which DITP holds employing advanced combinatorial techniques and measuretheoretic foundations Our analysis involves the exploration of overlapping sums defined over different classes of random variables revealing intricate relationships between their distributions and the manifestation of the DITP Additionally we illustrate practical applications of our findings through case studies that demonstrate how this property can facilitate enhanced decisionmaking processes in uncertain environments Our results not only contribute to the theoretical understanding of overlapping sums but also offer valuable insights for practitioners seeking to optimize outcomes across various domains We conclude by discussing avenues for future research including potential extensions of DITP and its implications in broader statistical contexts

author: Frank Proschan
text: In this paper we explore the interplay between uniform stochastic orderings and the concept of total positivity in the context of multivariate distributions Uniform stochastic ordering provides a robust framework for comparing random variables particularly in terms of their propensity to yield larger values under certain transformations We first establish a comprehensive theoretical foundation for uniform stochastic orders delving into their properties and implications for various classes of probability distributions Subsequently we investigate the relationship between these orderings and total positivity a mathematical property that characterizes the behavior of certain multivariate distributions and their associated positive dependence structures Through a series of examples and counterexamples we demonstrate how total positivity can inform our understanding of uniform stochastic dominance and vice versa Our findings contribute to the broader literature on stochastic ordering by offering new insights into the underlying mechanisms that govern dependence structures in random vectors and highlight potential applications in areas such as risk assessment decision theory and economics We conclude with a discussion of open questions and future directions for research in this intersecting field

author: Frank Proschan
text: In this paper we explore the characterization of nonparametric classes of life distributions which are crucial for statistical modeling and reliability analysis across various fields We begin by delineating the fundamental concepts of life distributions and their significance in survival analysis emphasizing the need for nonparametric approaches that do not impose stringent assumptions on the underlying data By employing empirical distribution functions and various stochastic orders we provide a comprehensive examination of nonparametric classes elucidating their properties and relationships Our analysis reveals the potential of these classes to capture diverse life patterns observed in realworld data facilitating a more flexible modeling framework We introduce several new nonparametric techniques for estimating life distributions supported by simulation studies that demonstrate their effectiveness and robustness in practical applications Furthermore we illustrate the utility of these methods through case studies involving medical and engineering data The findings contribute to the existing literature by offering a deeper understanding of nonparametric life distributions and presenting new avenues for future research in statistical methodology and applied statistics

author: Frank Proschan
text: In this paper a large class of multivariate densities and frequency functions including the multivariate Poisson distribution and the compound multivariate Poisson distribution are shown to have the decreasing in transposition property introduced by Hollander Proschan and Sethuraman Ann Statist Sample applications in ecology and reliability are given other applications to cumulation of damage and component down times are mentioned but are not presented in detail

author: Frank Proschan
text: In statistical modeling the presence of dependencies among variables often complicates analysis and inference This paper presents a novel framework for converting dependent models into independent ones while preserving essential features of the original data structure We introduce a twostep methodology first we identify and quantify the dependencies among variables using advanced graphical and statistical techniques Next we apply transformation algorithms that decouple these dependencies yielding independent models that retain critical characteristics such as marginal distributions and key associations among subsets of variables We validate our approach through a series of simulations demonstrating that our method effectively captures the underlying structure of complex datasets while facilitating straightforward analysis Applications of this technique are illustrated across several domains including finance genetics and social sciences emphasizing its utility in improving model interpretability and simplifying computational demands The findings illustrate significant potential for enhancing statistical practice by enabling researchers to leverage the simplicity of independent models without sacrificing the richness of dependent relationships

author: Frank Proschan
text: AbstractIn Bayesian statistics the posterior distribution is paramount for inference yet its dependence on the sample data often warrants further exploration This paper investigates the influence of sample characteristicssuch as size composition and variabilityon the resulting posterior distributions across a range of hierarchical and nonhierarchical modeling frameworks By employing simulation studies and realworld datasets we analyze how different sampling scenarios affect posterior estimates uncertainties and the robustness of inference Our findings reveal that smaller or biased samples can lead to significant shifts in posterior beliefs highlighting the potential for misleading inferences if sample data are not carefully considered Conversely we demonstrate how wellstructured sampling strategies can enhance the reliability of posterior distributions The study not only quantifies these influences but also provides practical recommendations for researchers to mitigate sampleinduced biases in Bayesian analysis Ultimately our results emphasize the critical role of sample selection in shaping effective and trustworthy Bayesian inference advancing the discussion on best practices for data collection and analysis in statistical research

author: Frank Proschan
text: A realvalued function g g of two vector arguments x x and y R n y is said to be arrangement increasing if it increases in value as the arrangement of components in x x becomes increasingly similar to the arrangement of components in y y Hollander Proschan and Sethuraman show that the convolution of arrangement increasing functions is arrangement increasing This result is used to generate some interesting probability inequalities of a geometric nature for exchangeable random vectors Other geometric inequalities for families of arrangement increasing multivariate densities are also given and some moment inequalities are obtained

author: Frank Proschan
text: In this paper we explore the role of Schur functions within the context of statistical theory presenting a comprehensive examination of their properties and applications We introduce a novel preservation theorem that establishes the conditions under which the Schur functions retain their fundamental characteristics when applied to certain statistical transformations The theorem is built upon a rigorous mathematical framework and is demonstrated through a series of illustrative examples that highlight its relevance in statistical inference and data analysis Additionally we discuss the implications of our findings for multivariate distributions providing a deeper understanding of the interactions between Schur functions and statistical measures By bridging the gap between combinatorial theory and statistical methodology our results enhance the toolkit available to researchers and practitioners working with complex data structures This work lays the groundwork for future studies that may further investigate the utility of Schur functions in various statistical contexts paving the way for innovative analytical approaches

author: Frank Proschan
text: This paper presents a comprehensive study on the estimation of parameters for a multivariate exponential distribution a continuous probability distribution that generalizes the exponential distribution to multiple dimensions We explore various estimation techniques including maximum likelihood estimation MLE and Bayesian inference to derive robust parameter estimates under different sample sizes and correlation structures Theoretical properties such as consistency and asymptotic normality of the estimators are derived and discussed Simulation studies are conducted to evaluate the performance of the proposed methods highlighting the impact of sample size and dimensionality on estimation accuracy Additionally we apply our framework to realworld datasets demonstrating the practical applicability of multivariate exponential models in fields such as survival analysis and reliability engineering Our findings contribute to a deeper understanding of multivariate exponential distributions and provide a foundation for their use in complex data analysis scenarios

author: Frank Proschan
text: Parameter estimation for a k parameter version of the kdimensional multivariate exponential distribution MVE of Marshall and Olkin is investigated Although not absolutely continuous with respect to Lebesgue measure a density with respect to a dominating measure is specified enabling derivation of a likelihood function and likelihood equations In general the likelihood equations not solvable explicitly have a unique root which is the maximum likelihood estimator MLE A simple estimator INT is derived as the first iterate in solving the likelihood equations iteratively The resulting sequence of estimators converges to the MLE for sufficiently large samples These results can be extended to the more general k parameter MVE

author: Frank Proschan
text: Let F F denote the life distribution of a coherent structure of independent components Suppose that we have a sample of independent systems all having the same structure Each system is continuously observed until it fails For every component in each system either a failure time or a censoring time is recorded A failure time is recorded if the component fails before or at the time of system failure otherwise a censoring time is recorded We introduce a method for finding estimates for Ft F quantiles and other functionals of F F based on the censorship of the component lives by system failure We use the theory of counting processes and stochastic integrals to obtain limit theorems that enable the construction of confidence intervals for large samples Our approach extends and gives a novel application of censoring methodology

author: Frank Proschan
text: In this paper we investigate the Schur convexity properties of the maximumlikelihood function for the multivariate hypergeometric and multinomial distributions Schur convexity is an important concept in the study of inequalities and order theory particularly within the context of multivariate statistics We first establish the necessary theoretical framework for Schur convexity and its implications for the likelihood functions associated with these two discrete distributions By analyzing the structure of their maximumlikelihood estimators we demonstrate that the likelihood functions exhibit Schur convexity which implies that the probability of obtaining larger outcomes increases with respect to majorization of parameter vectors We apply combinatorial techniques and inequalities to derive conditions under which the maximumlikelihood function maintains this convex ordering Our findings not only enhance the understanding of the statistical properties of these distributions but also contribute to the broader discourse on the implications of Schur convexity in statistical inference The results have significant applications in fields such as ecology genetics and quality control where multivariate count data is prevalent Detailed proofs and examples illustrate the practical relevance of our theoretical contributions providing a robust foundation for further research into the implications of Schur convexity in multivariate statistical models

author: Frank Proschan
text: In this paper we introduce and explore the concept of multivariate arrangement increasing functions MAIFs a class of functions that generalizes classical increasing functions to multiple dimensions We define MAIFs through their preservation of ordering across multivariate inputs and investigate their properties including continuity convexity and their behavior under transformations We establish key results that illustrate the relationship between MAIFs and established statistical concepts such as copulas concordance and stochastic dominance Furthermore we demonstrate practical applications of MAIFs in probability and statistics particularly in the realms of multivariate regression analysis risk assessment and model sensitivity By employing MAIFs we provide new insights into the behavior of multivariate distributions enhance the understanding of dependence structures and facilitate the development of robust statistical methodologies Our findings not only expand the theoretical framework of multivariate analysis but also offer practitioners useful tools for data analysis and decisionmaking in complex systems

author: Frank Proschan
text: In this paper we introduce a straightforward statistical test designed to assess the concept of new better than used in expectation NBUE This property which plays a crucial role in reliability theory and decisionmaking posits that new items are statistically expected to perform better than used items on average Our method leverages basic statistical tools to evaluate the comparative performance of two populations new and used items through a welldefined hypothesis testing framework We derive the critical conditions under which NBUE holds and provide practical guidance on implementing our test using realworld data Simulation studies demonstrate the effectiveness of our test in various scenarios highlighting its robustness and simplicity By offering an accessible approach to this complex statistical issue our work aims to facilitate the evaluation of performance characteristics in numerous applications ranging from manufacturing to consumer product analysis The implications of adopting this testing methodology extend to better decisionmaking in both academic and industrial contexts

text: In reliability engineering accurately estimating the reliability of complex systems and their individual components is crucial for effective risk management and decisionmaking This paper introduces a novel statistical approach for estimating joint system and component reliabilities by employing a mutual censorship framework In our proposed method we leverage the interdependencies between system components and the simultaneous failure data to achieve a more accurate and coherent reliability estimation We establish a probabilistic model that captures the inherent dependencies among components while accounting for the censoring effects typically encountered in reliability data Through simulations and realworld case studies we illustrate the efficacy of our method in providing reliable estimates compared to traditional approaches The results demonstrate that the mutual censorship approach yields improved precision and resolves potential biases in reliability estimates thus providing a valuable tool for practitioners in the field Our findings underscore the importance of considering joint reliability within interconnected systems and highlight the potential for enhanced decisionmaking processes in reliability analysis

author: Frank Proschan
text: In many combinatorial optimization contexts selection problems play a crucial role in making optimal choices from a set of candidates based on specific criteria This paper introduces a unified framework to analyze the monotonicity properties inherent in a broad class of selection problems By rigorously defining monotonicity within these contexts we explore its implications for algorithm design and performance guarantees Our approach offers a comprehensive classification of monotonicity types including strong weak and conditional monotonicity and demonstrates how these definitions simplify the analysis of various selection algorithms We illustrate the applicability of our theoretical results through case studies in resource allocation ranking systems and multicriteria decisionmaking scenarios Additionally we provide insights into how monotonicity can lead to more efficient algorithmic solutions while minimizing computational complexity The results presented pave the way for further exploration of monotonic properties in related optimization tasks fostering advancements in both theoretical understanding and practical implementations

author: Frank Proschan
text: A real valued function of s vector arguments in Rn is said to be arrangement increasing if the function increases in value as the components of the vector arguments become more similarly arranged Various examples of arrangement increasing functions are given including many joint multivariate densities measures of concordance between judges and the permanent of a matrix with nonnegative components Preservation properties of the class of arrangement increasing functions are examined and applications are given including useful probabilistic inequalities for linear combinations of exchangeable random vectors

text: We generalize a covariance inequality for coherent structures We replace the earlier assumption of independence among components by association a weaker assumption applicable to many situations encountered in practice The proof of the more general result turns out to be simpler than that of the earlier more restricted case

text: This paper presents a novel inequality concerning covariance structures within the framework of coherent random fields We begin by establishing the fundamental properties of coherent structures which are characterized by their inherent symmetries and interdependencies Utilizing advanced probabilistic techniques and matrix theory we derive a covariance inequality that provides insights into the relationships between different random variables within these structures Our results extend existing inequalities in multivariate statistics offering both theoretical advancements and practical implications for fields such as spatial statistics finance and risk assessment We validate our findings through simulations and realworld data applications demonstrating the relevance of this inequality in understanding variability and dependence in coherent systems The implications of our work pave the way for further research in covariance analysis in more complex statistical models

author: Frank Proschan
text: This paper investigates the hypothesis of exponentiality in lifetime data in the presence of potential trends in the mean residual life function The mean residual life MRL is a pivotal concept in reliability analysis and survival studies as it provides insights into the expected remaining lifespan of an object or individual given its current age We propose a new statistical testing framework to differentiate between a simple exponential distribution and a timevarying mean residual life model that reflects a trend change Our approach leverages both graphical methods and formal statistical tests that are robust to small sample sizes and variations in data characteristics We apply the proposed testing framework to several realworld datasets demonstrating its efficacy in detecting deviations from exponentiality and identifying trends in MRL The findings reveal that traditional methods may overlook significant underlying patterns in lifetimes suggesting that attention to nonexponentiality is crucial in reliability assessments and life data analysis The implications of our results extend to various fields including engineering medicine and economics where understanding the nature of life distributions is vital for decisionmaking and resource allocation

author: Frank Proschan
text: In this paper we extend the foundational principles of Schur functions in the context of statistical theory focusing specifically on the concept of stochastic majorization Stochastic majorization provides a framework for comparing random variables based on their distributional properties and moments allowing us to make meaningful statistical inferences about inequality and variability We explore the relationship between Schur functions and stochastic majorization by examining how these mathematical constructs can be utilized to characterize and assess the relative performance of statistical estimators and models Through a series of theoretical developments and illustrative examples we demonstrate the utility of Schur functions in establishing majorization inequalities thereby enabling a nuanced understanding of the behavior of statistical properties under various transformations Our findings have implications for the field of inequality measurement providing new insights into the performance of aggregate statistical measures across different distributions This work contributes to the growing intersection between algebraic combinatorics and statistical theory and sets the stage for future research on the applications of Schur functions in statistical analysis

author: Frank Proschan
text: In this paper we explore the role of Schur functions within the context of statistical theory presenting a comprehensive examination of their properties and applications We introduce a novel preservation theorem that establishes the conditions under which the Schur functions retain their fundamental characteristics when applied to certain statistical transformations The theorem is built upon a rigorous mathematical framework and is demonstrated through a series of illustrative examples that highlight its relevance in statistical inference and data analysis Additionally we discuss the implications of our findings for multivariate distributions providing a deeper understanding of the interactions between Schur functions and statistical measures By bridging the gap between combinatorial theory and statistical methodology our results enhance the toolkit available to researchers and practitioners working with complex data structures This work lays the groundwork for future studies that may further investigate the utility of Schur functions in various statistical contexts paving the way for innovative analytical approaches

author: Frank Proschan
text: In the realm of survival analysis accurately estimating dependent life lengths is crucial for understanding the dynamics of competing risks This paper presents a novel statistical framework for estimating life lengths when multiple dependent risks are present extending traditional survival models that often assume independence among competing events We introduce a joint modeling approach that combines elements of copula theory and frailty models enabling us to capture the inherent dependence between competing risks while providing robust estimates of survival probabilities and hazard functions We apply our methodology to realworld datasets from healthcare studies where the risks of different medical conditions interact demonstrating the effectiveness of our approach in revealing nuanced insights into patient outcomes Our findings highlight the importance of accounting for dependency in risk estimation and we discuss implications for both statistical methodology and practical applications in fields such as biostatistics and actuarial science Ultimately this work contributes to a deeper understanding of competing risks and offers enhanced tools for researchers and practitioners aiming to inform decisionmaking in complex risk environments

author: Frank Proschan
text: In the classical theory of competing risks as well as in many reliability models and incomplete data problems it is assumed that A the risks ie the random variables of interest are independent and that A death does not result from simultaneous causes Employing our probabilistic solution to a related problem in probability modelling we obtain strongly consistent estimators for the unobservable marginal distributions of interest These estimators are analogous to those of Kaplan and Meier and are appropriate when the assumptions of independence and no simultaneous causes of death fail to hold We show how our methods can be used to unify and simplify the nonparametric approach toward estimation in the competing risks model As a consequence we obtain an elementary proof of the strong consistency of the KaplanMeier estimator Our results extend and simplify the work of Peterson and Desu and Narula

author: Frank Proschan
text: In statistical modeling the presence of dependencies among variables often complicates analysis and inference This paper presents a novel framework for converting dependent models into independent ones while preserving essential features of the original data structure We introduce a twostep methodology first we identify and quantify the dependencies among variables using advanced graphical and statistical techniques Next we apply transformation algorithms that decouple these dependencies yielding independent models that retain critical characteristics such as marginal distributions and key associations among subsets of variables We validate our approach through a series of simulations demonstrating that our method effectively captures the underlying structure of complex datasets while facilitating straightforward analysis Applications of this technique are illustrated across several domains including finance genetics and social sciences emphasizing its utility in improving model interpretability and simplifying computational demands The findings illustrate significant potential for enhancing statistical practice by enabling researchers to leverage the simplicity of independent models without sacrificing the richness of dependent relationships

author: Frank Proschan
text: Given that an item is of age t the expected value of the random remaining life is called the mean residual life MRL at age t We propose two new nonparametric classes of life distributions for modeling aging based on MRL The first class of life distributions consists of those with increasing initially then decreasing mean residual life IDMRL The IDMRL class models aging that is initially beneficial then adverse The second class decreasing then increasing mean residual life DIMRL models aging that is initially adverse then beneficial We propose two testing procedures for H constant MRL ie exponentiality versus H IDMRL but not constant MRL or H DIMRL but not constant MRL The first testing procedure assumes the turning point from IMRL to DMRL is specified by the user or is known The second procedure assumes knowledge of the proportion of the population that dies at or before the turning point knowledge of itself is not assumed

author: Frank Proschan
text: Earlier papers have shown how to convert competing risk models involving dependent random variables into models involving only independent random variables while simultaneously preserving the distribution of the minimum and the probabilities of the various failure patterns In the present paper we consider a sequence of such conversions occurring at successive points in chronological time in which the independent random variables are becoming stochastically larger We obtain results which essentially demonstrate that the limiting distributions in the sequence of dependent models correctly correspond to the limiting distributions in the sequence of independent models These results have applications in reliability growth models and in biomedical competing risk models in which the competing risks are increasing with age in these models dependency is permitted among the random variables

author: Frank Proschan
text: In this paper we investigate the Schur convexity properties of the maximumlikelihood function for the multivariate hypergeometric and multinomial distributions Schur convexity is an important concept in the study of inequalities and order theory particularly within the context of multivariate statistics We first establish the necessary theoretical framework for Schur convexity and its implications for the likelihood functions associated with these two discrete distributions By analyzing the structure of their maximumlikelihood estimators we demonstrate that the likelihood functions exhibit Schur convexity which implies that the probability of obtaining larger outcomes increases with respect to majorization of parameter vectors We apply combinatorial techniques and inequalities to derive conditions under which the maximumlikelihood function maintains this convex ordering Our findings not only enhance the understanding of the statistical properties of these distributions but also contribute to the broader discourse on the implications of Schur convexity in statistical inference The results have significant applications in fields such as ecology genetics and quality control where multivariate count data is prevalent Detailed proofs and examples illustrate the practical relevance of our theoretical contributions providing a robust foundation for further research into the implications of Schur convexity in multivariate statistical models

text: In this paper we obtain characterizations of large classes of nonparametric life distributions such as the increasing decreasing failure rate increasing decreasing failure rate average new better worse than used etc classes The methods used differ from the usual functional equation methods used for the far more common characterizations of parametric families of life distributions

author: Frank Proschan
text: In this paper we introduce a novel framework for understanding and quantifying associations among multiple variables through the concept of generalized association While conventional association measures typically address bivariate relationships our approach extends these concepts to encompass multivariate scenarios providing a rigorous statistical foundation for analyzing interactions within highdimensional data We develop a set of generalized association metrics that capture both linear and nonlinear dependencies enabling researchers to uncover complex relationships that traditional methods may overlook Through extensive simulations and realdata applications we demonstrate the utility of our proposed metrics in various contexts such as psychometrics genomics and environmental studies We also present a comprehensive set of tools for visualizing multivariate associations including scatterplot matrices and heatmaps which facilitate the interpretation of intricate relationships among multiple variables Our findings suggest that generalized association metrics significantly enhance the detectability of underlying patterns in multivariate datasets paving the way for more informed decisionmaking in fields reliant on complex data analysis This work lays the groundwork for future research and methodology enhancements in the field of multivariate statistics

text: In this paper we explore the characterization of nonparametric classes of life distributions which are crucial for statistical modeling and reliability analysis across various fields We begin by delineating the fundamental concepts of life distributions and their significance in survival analysis emphasizing the need for nonparametric approaches that do not impose stringent assumptions on the underlying data By employing empirical distribution functions and various stochastic orders we provide a comprehensive examination of nonparametric classes elucidating their properties and relationships Our analysis reveals the potential of these classes to capture diverse life patterns observed in realworld data facilitating a more flexible modeling framework We introduce several new nonparametric techniques for estimating life distributions supported by simulation studies that demonstrate their effectiveness and robustness in practical applications Furthermore we illustrate the utility of these methods through case studies involving medical and engineering data The findings contribute to the existing literature by offering a deeper understanding of nonparametric life distributions and presenting new avenues for future research in statistical methodology and applied statistics

author: Frank Proschan
text: In reliability engineering KoutofN systems serve as fundamental models for assessing the performance and dependability of complex systems comprised of interconnected components This paper delves into the reliability characteristics of KoutofN systems focusing on both theoretical foundations and practical implications We present a comprehensive analysis of the systems reliability function incorporating various failure distributions and dependencies among components By employing advanced statistical techniques we derive explicit expressions for the reliability and failure probabilities and we explore the impact of component redundancy on overall system performance Furthermore we utilize Monte Carlo simulations to validate our theoretical results and provide insights into the systems behavior under diverse operational conditions Our findings demonstrate that the reliability of KoutofN systems is significantly influenced by the choice of components and their arrangement revealing optimal strategies for design and maintenance This study contributes to a deeper understanding of reliability metrics in engineering and informs decisionmaking processes regarding system design in various applications from telecommunications to aerospace engineering We conclude with implications for future research and potential advancements in reliability assessment methodologies

author: Frank Proschan
text: In recent years the analysis of degradable systems has garnered significant interest due to its implications in various fields including engineering reliability assessment and risk management This paper presents a comprehensive survey of multistate system theory as applied to degradable systems where the performance can dynamically transition between multiple states due to aging wear or external stress factors We systematically review the foundational concepts key models and analytical methodologies that characterize the behavior of multistate systems emphasizing their relevance in understanding degradation processes Our study encompasses classic reliability models including multistate Markov processes and stochastic finite state machines while also addressing recent advancements in the field such as fuzzy logic and machine learning approaches for predictive maintenance Furthermore we explore various applications ranging from industrial systems to ecological models highlighting how multistate frameworks enhance the understanding of system resilience and life cycle management By synthesizing existing literature and identifying emerging trends this survey aims to provide a solid groundwork for future research in multistate system theory and its applications to degradable systems ultimately contributing to more reliable and sustainable system design

author: Frank Proschan
text: Association of random variables is generalized by considering increasing functions on certain partially ordered spaces Generalized association enjoys many of the basic properties possessed by association An essential connection links the two notions Generalized association is inherited under certain mixing processes Applications of this result follow for absolute value ordering unimodal ordering and linear ordering of the real numbers

author: Frank Proschan
text: AbstractIn Bayesian statistics the posterior distribution is paramount for inference yet its dependence on the sample data often warrants further exploration This paper investigates the influence of sample characteristicssuch as size composition and variabilityon the resulting posterior distributions across a range of hierarchical and nonhierarchical modeling frameworks By employing simulation studies and realworld datasets we analyze how different sampling scenarios affect posterior estimates uncertainties and the robustness of inference Our findings reveal that smaller or biased samples can lead to significant shifts in posterior beliefs highlighting the potential for misleading inferences if sample data are not carefully considered Conversely we demonstrate how wellstructured sampling strategies can enhance the reliability of posterior distributions The study not only quantifies these influences but also provides practical recommendations for researchers to mitigate sampleinduced biases in Bayesian analysis Ultimately our results emphasize the critical role of sample selection in shaping effective and trustworthy Bayesian inference advancing the discussion on best practices for data collection and analysis in statistical research

author: Frank Proschan
text: A system with n n independent components which functions if and only if at least k k of the components function is a k k out of n n system Parallel systems are out of n n systems and series systems are n n out of n n systems If p p p n p is the vector of component reliabilities for the n n components then h k p h is the reliability function of the system It is shown that h k p h is Schurconvex in n n n n p This Theorem is compared with a result on Schurconvexity and concavity by Gleser which in turn extends work of Hoeffding

author: Frank Proschan
text: The vast majority of reliability analyses assume that ccmponents and system are in either of two states functioning or failed However in many real life situations we are actually able to distinguish among various Ilevels of performance for both system and components For such situations the existing dichotomous model is a gross oversimplification and so models assuming degradable multistate systems and components are preferable since they are closer to realityWe present a survey of recent papers which treat the more I sophisticated and more realistic models in which components and systems may assume many states ranging from perfect functioning to complete failure Our survey updates and complements a previous survey by ElNeweihi and Proschan Some new results are included
